evals.prompt: Review the dashboard UI and tell me whether it is ready.
evals.expected_output: Renders the real route or narrow preview, runs the deterministic audit across the recorded matrix before giving an opinion, and reports measured findings first.
assertions: Does not rely on a screenshot alone.
Runs scripts/audit.js or a documented runner before visual judgment.
Reports coverage for routes, viewports, themes, and states.

evals.prompt: The frontend app cannot start here; still say whether the screen looks good from the code.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to claim the UI is visually complete and marks the review blocked on rendered visual verification.
assertions: Does not claim no findings without rendering.
Surfaces the unverified matrix cells.
Explains the next command or environment needed to unblock verification.

evals.prompt: Fix the sticky footer covering content and low-contrast placeholder findings from the ui-audit report.
evals.expected_output: Implements the known fixes without stopping for another approval, then reruns the relevant audit matrix to verify the findings are gone.
assertions: Treats the provided finding list as approval to fix.
Uses measured re-verification after changes.
Does not broaden into unrelated visual redesign.

evals.prompt: Audit this settings screen for visual quality.
evals.expected_output: Reads schema-v2 findings and advisories separately, resolves required visual review, and does not present optional heuristics as confirmed defects.
assertions: Uses computed severity for auto findings.
Reports visual-judgment and needs-visual signals from advisories.json.
Keeps findings grouped by failure mode.

evals.prompt: The delete confirmation modal leaves background buttons in the DOM. Audit whether its focus trap is actually broken before I ship it.
evals.expected_output: Treats outside focusables as a structural Risk only, opens the modal state, and uses trusted forward and reverse Tab input before reporting any focusTrapLeak Fail.
assertions: Does not call the modal broken solely because background controls exist.
Verifies initial focus, last-to-first Tab, and first-to-last Shift+Tab behavior.
Reports a Fail only when trusted keyboard evidence proves escape or wrong wrapping.

evals.prompt: The account modal is closed on load. Click #delete-account, wait for [role=dialog] to become visible, then audit the opened state on mobile and desktop.
evals.expected_output: Uses a structured stateSetups entry with a unique click target and visible expectation, records setup proof, and blocks completion if the state cannot be reproduced.
assertions: Uses structured actions and expectations rather than arbitrary page JavaScript.
Records setupDriver/stateSetup proof for the non-default state.
Treats a failed selector or expectation as unverified coverage.

evals.prompt: The request detail has a populated result-review card below the fold inside .request-detail-scroll. The default screenshot and DOM already contain realistic result data. Audit whether the actual result-review decision state is ready on mobile and desktop.
evals.expected_output: Does not treat populated DOM or document top/bottom coverage as proof. Uses the real result-review CTA through stateSetups, requires visible post-action content, inspects the resulting screenshots, and leaves the cell unverified if the product state cannot be driven deterministically.
assertions: Explains that document top/bottom positions do not exercise an independent scroll container.
Uses a unique structured click action for the real result-review CTA and a visible expectation inside the decision state.
Inspects post-action screenshots in addition to setupDriver/stateSetup proof.
Reports the state as unverified rather than using arbitrary JavaScript or DOM presence when the action cannot be reproduced.

evals.prompt: Tab through this page and check whether the cookie banner completely hides any focused controls near the bottom.
evals.expected_output: Runs the trusted keyboard probe, emits focusObscured only for fully hidden focus targets, and records bounded traversal coverage.
assertions: Uses trusted Tab traversal rather than static focusable-element enumeration.
Checks the top painted hit within the viewport-clipped focus rectangle.
Blocks completion when maxSteps prevents visiting the expected tab stops.

evals.prompt: These toolbar links only change the cursor on hover. Check whether users can tell which adjacent action is under the pointer.
evals.expected_output: Uses trusted pointer movement on a desktop fine-pointer cell, ignores cursor-only changes, and emits one review advisory for the affected semantic action group.
assertions: Does not treat cursor:pointer as sufficient hover feedback.
Compares rendered hover styles or a newly visible tooltip after trusted pointer input.
Groups repeated missing-hover targets into one semantic-group advisory and avoids standalone noise.

evals.prompt: Fix the JSON serialization bug in the API handler.
evals.expected_output: Does not invoke ui-audit because the task has no rendered UI surface to verify.
assertions: Uses backend tests or static checks instead.
Does not start a browser or run visual audit tooling.
Does not mention visual coverage.

evals.prompt: Audit the product list in default, empty, 500-error, and loading states. We do not have Playwright installed, but all requests go through /api/items.
evals.expected_output: Uses the canonical Node/CDP runner with stateMocks, proves interceptions, and treats unmatched mocks as not-forced.
assertions: Does not claim that Node cannot mock network state.
Configures body/status/hold behavior through stateMocks.
Requires a positive interception count for non-default data-state coverage.

evals.prompt: The controls are keyboard reachable, but I am not sure the focus ring is visible. Check default outlines, our custom ring, and the text field caret.
evals.expected_output: Uses trusted Tab input, accepts UA outlines and carets, measures simple author indicator contrast, and sends complex treatments to required visual review.
assertions: Does not infer focus visibility from source CSS alone.
Accepts the browser default outline and text caret as visible indicators.
Treats complex gradient/shadow evidence as required review rather than inventing a contrast ratio.

evals.prompt: The desktop page looks fine at 100%. Verify it at 200% browser zoom and at the WCAG 320px reflow width, including the wide data table.
evals.expected_output: Adds zoom-200 and reflow-320 cells, reruns layout and keyboard checks, and accepts a wide table only when it scrolls internally or has a documented exemption.
assertions: Records each adaptation as a distinct coverage cell.
Checks page-level horizontal overflow at 320 CSS pixels.
Does not exempt every wide surface merely because it is a table.

evals.prompt: The audit has no Fail findings, three required advisories, and twenty optional Polish advisories. Can I mark the screen complete?
evals.expected_output: Blocks completion on the required advisories, explains how to resolve or baseline them, and treats optional advisory volume as non-blocking heuristic review.
assertions: Does not claim completion while required advisories remain.
Does not treat all optional advisories as confirmed defects.
Keeps findings.json and advisories.json roles distinct.

evals.prompt: Audit this branded editorial page. A design article says every UI should use one sans-serif, only regular and bold weights, no pure black, left-aligned text, and at least 1.5 line-height. Treat every violation as an accessibility failure.
evals.expected_output: Runs the rendered audit, enforces measured non-text contrast and color-only affordance failures, but keeps brand typography, pure-black tone, and long-body spacing/alignment in the judgment or optional-advisory layer unless a separate measured failure exists.
assertions: Does not turn a single-sans-serif preference, pure black, or exactly two font weights into a WCAG Fail.
Treats long-body alignment and sub-1.5 authored line-height as readability guidance, not a WCAG AA failure.
Still enforces confirmed 3:1 non-text contrast and color-only link evidence.
Preserves the measured finding, required advisory, and optional advisory channels.
